units.text: INT. HUSBAND - CONTINUOUS
Oh, I love London Society! I think it has immensely improved. It is entirely composed now of beautiful idiots and brilliant lunatics. Just what Society should be.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Hum! Which is Goring? Beautiful idiot, or the other thing?
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Gravely .
I have been obliged for the present to put Lord Goring into a class quite by himself. But he is developing charmingly!
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Into what?
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: With a little curtsey .
I hope to let you know very soon, Lord Caversham!
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Announcing guests .
Lady Markby. Mrs. Cheveley.
units.name: MASON

units.text: Enter LADY MARKBY and MRS. CHEVELEY.
LADY MARKBY is a pleasant , kindly , popular woman , with gray hair à la marquise and good lace .
MRS. CHEVELEY, who accompanies her , is tall and rather slight .
Lips very thin and highly-coloured , a line of scarlet on a pallid face .
Venetian red hair , aquiline nose , and long throat .
Rouge accentuates the natural paleness of her complexion .
Gray-green eyes that move restlessly .
She is in heliotrope , with diamonds .
She looks rather like an orchid , and makes great demands on one’s curiosity .
In all her movements she is extremely graceful .
A work of art , on the whole , but showing the influence of too many schools .
Good evening, dear Gertrude! So kind of you to let me bring my friend, Mrs. Cheveley. Two such charming women should know each other!
units.name: LADY MARKBY

units.text: Advances towards MRS. CHEVELEY with a sweet smile .
Then suddenly stops , and bows rather distantly .
I think Mrs. Cheveley and I have met before. I did not know she had married a second time.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Genially .
Ah, nowadays people marry as often as they can, don’t they? It is most fashionable.
units.name: LADY MARKBY

units.text: To DUCHESS OF MARYBOROUGH.
Dear Duchess, and how is the Duke? Brain still weak, I suppose? Well, that is only to be expected, is it not? His good father was just the same. There is nothing like race, is there?
units.name: LADY MARKBY

units.text: Playing with her fan .
But have we really met before, Lady Chiltern? I can’t remember where. I have been out of England for so long.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: We were at school together, Mrs. Cheveley.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: CHEVELEY
units.name: MRS

units.text: Superciliously .
Indeed? I have forgotten all about my schooldays. I have a vague impression that they were detestable.
units.name: MRS

units.text: Coldly .
I am not surprised!
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: In her sweetest manner .

Do you know, I am quite looking forward to meeting your clever husband, Lady Chiltern. Since he has been at the Foreign Office, he has been so much talked of in Vienna. They actually succeed in spelling his name right in the newspapers. That in itself is fame, on the continent.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: I hardly think there will be much in common between you and my husband, Mrs. Cheveley!
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Moves away .
Ah! chère Madame, quelle surprise! I have not seen you since Berlin!
units.name: VICOMTE DE NANJAC

units.text: Not since Berlin, Vicomte. Five years ago!
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: And you are younger and more beautiful than ever. How do you manage it?
units.name: VICOMTE DE NANJAC

units.text: By making it a rule only to talk to perfectly charming people like yourself.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Ah! you flatter me. You butter me, as they say here.
units.name: VICOMTE DE NANJAC

units.text: Do they say that here? How dreadful of them!
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Yes, they have a wonderful language. It should be more widely known.
units.name: VICOMTE DE NANJAC

units.text: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN enters .
A man of forty , but looking somewhat younger .
Clean-shaven , with finely-cut features , dark-haired and dark-eyed .
A personality of mark .
Not popular—few personalities are .
But intensely admired by the few , and deeply respected by the many .
The note of his manner is that of perfect distinction , with a slight touch of pride .
One feels that he is conscious of the success he has made in life .
A nervous temperament , with a tired look .
The firmly-chiselled mouth and chin contrast strikingly with the romantic expression in the deep-set eyes .
The variance is suggestive of an almost complete separation of passion and intellect , as though thought and emotion were each isolated in its own sphere through some violence of will-power .
There is nervousness in the nostrils , and in the pale , thin , pointed hands .
It would be inaccurate to call him picturesque .
Picturesqueness cannot survive the House of Commons .
But Vandyck would have liked to have painted his head .
Good evening, Lady Markby! I hope you have brought Sir John with you?
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Oh! I have brought a much more charming person than Sir John. Sir John’s temper since he has taken seriously to politics has become quite unbearable. Really, now that the House of Commons is trying to become useful, it does a great deal of harm.
units.name: LADY MARKBY

units.text: I hope not, Lady Markby. At any rate we do our best to waste the public time, don’t we? But who is this charming person you have been kind enough to bring to us?
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Her name is Mrs. Cheveley! One of the Dorsetshire Cheveleys, I suppose. But I really don’t know. Families are so mixed nowadays. Indeed, as a rule, everybody turns out to be somebody else.
units.name: LADY MARKBY

units.text: Mrs. Cheveley? I seem to know the name.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: She has just arrived from Vienna.
units.name: LADY MARKBY

units.text: Ah! yes. I think I know whom you mean.
units.name: SIR ROBERT CHILTERN

units.text: Oh! she goes everywhere there, and has such pleasant scandals about all her friends. I really must go to Vienna next winter. I hope there is a good chef at the Embassy.
units.name: LADY MARKBY
